risk_if_not_implemented: Without Compliance As Code (CAC) Identity Governance, automated control assurance results may be manipulated, misattributed or lose integrity, causing misplaced confidence in control effectiveness. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities (R-GV-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Identity & Access Management (IAM)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of Identification and Access Management (IAM) controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Identity & Access Management (IAM) (IAC-02) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Compliance As Code (CAC) Identity Governance (IAC-50) by restricting system and data access through alternative identity and access management mechanisms. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Periodic Review of Individual & Service Account Privileges
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to periodically-review the privileges assigned to individuals and service accounts to validate the need for such privileges and reassign or remove unnecessary privileges, as necessary.
compensating_control_2.justification: Periodic Review of Individual & Service Account Privileges (IAC-12) provides periodic assessment and verification that compensates for the absence of Compliance As Code (CAC) Identity Governance (IAC-50) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
